items.title: Show HN: TokenMaxxer – track every AI token you spend across your coding tools
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer built a CLI tool and dashboard to track token usage and costs across coding tools like Claude Code and Codex. Since you use these tools daily and want to keep your development costs down, this gives you a clear picture of your actual API spend. This week, install the TokenMaxxer CLI to analyze how many tokens your AI-ingest project has consumed so far.

items.title: Show HN: An AI-Powered Widget for Collecting User Feedback

items.title: VibeMenu – a local macOS menu-bar dashboard for Claude Code and Codex
items.why_it_matters: A developer built a local macOS menu-bar dashboard specifically for managing Claude Code and Codex sessions. If you are tired of losing track of your active terminal sessions while vibe coding, this puts your active agents directly in your menu bar. This week, clone the repository and run it locally to streamline how you trigger and monitor Claude Code on your laptop.

items.title: Show HN: Gitleaks for Codex and Claude Code
items.why_it_matters: A new utility integrates Gitleaks directly with Codex and Claude Code to prevent you from accidentally committing API keys. Since AI-ingest is your first repository where you are practicing real Git discipline, securing your Supabase and Anthropic keys is a critical step. This week, run this tool on your local AI-ingest repository to verify that no active credentials have slipped into your commit history.

items.title: Show HN: AgentCodeGUI – Multi-Account Desktop GUI for Claude Code and Codex
items.why_it_matters: A developer built a desktop GUI for Claude Code and Codex that lets you manage files, run multiple agents, and easily switch between different accounts when you hit rate limits. If you find yourself drowning in terminal windows while directing your AI, this organizes your workspace into a single interface. This week, download the GUI and use it to run your next coding session for AI-ingest.
